result:
I graded Riley's submission s1 for quiz 0001: 2 correct, 2 partial, 2 wrong. The grades are in `grades/0001-s1.json`.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Wrong (M4) | The model outputs a request naming `check_calendar`. It doesn't open the booking system itself. |
| q3 | Correct | A step limit is the right safeguard for a stuck loop. |
| q4 | Wrong (M4) | The answer is 4 model calls. Riley said 1, because they thought the model runs the three tools itself. |
| q5 | Partial | "It sends it back to the model" covers what happens. It leaves out why: so the model can pick its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | Partial (M3) | Riley was right that the model picks a tool from the descriptions it's given. They were wrong that it remembers earlier sessions on its own. |

**What Riley has down:** the shape of the agent loop, when to stop it, and that the model chooses tools from their descriptions.

**What to work on:** the model only writes requests, and the program runs the tools. Memory isn't automatic either: the program has to save information and put it back into the model's input.

**Next step:** Riley should redo the q4 makerspace question as "model outputs … / program does …" steps and recount the model calls. After that, context and memory is the next topic, and it answers the q6 gap.

I also added `learning-records/0003-model-does-not-run-tools.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. The second attempt, `submissions/s2.json`, is still ungraded. I can grade it next if you want.
